sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
LMN-301 (illustrative): an intranasal spray of spirulina-produced binding proteins intended to neutralise a respiratory virus at the nasal mucosa.

This report describes DEMO-LMN301-P2A-CHAL-001, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled human viral challenge study conducted in quarantine in healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years, seronegative or with a low neutralising titre to the challenge strain. Prevention of viral upper respiratory infection (human challenge model) is the target of the programme; this study was designed to evaluate whether prophylactic intranasal LMN-301 reduces laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after viral challenge compared with placebo.

sections.title: Study Objectives
sections.content:
Primary objective:

  • To evaluate whether prophylactic intranasal LMN-301 reduces laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after viral challenge compared with placebo.

Secondary objectives:

  • To evaluate the effect of LMN-301 on viral shedding.
  • To describe the safety and local tolerability of intranasal LMN-301.

Exploratory objectives:

  • To describe body temperature and inflammatory markers after challenge.

sections.title: Discussion of Study Design, Including the Choice of Control Groups
sections.content: A placebo intranasal arm was used so that adverse events and outcomes could be attributed to the investigational product rather than to the course of the condition, the study procedures or expectation. Blinding (section 9.4.6) protects the comparison.

sections.title: Selection of Study Population
sections.content: The study enrolled healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years, seronegative or with a low neutralising titre to the challenge strain.

sections.title: Inclusion Criteria
sections.content:
Participants were eligible if they met all of the following:

  • Healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years.
  • A serum neutralising antibody titre to the challenge strain at or below the protocol threshold at screening.
  • Willing to remain in quarantine from Day -2 to Day 8.
  • Able to give written informed consent.

sections.title: Exclusion Criteria
sections.content:
Participants were not eligible if any of the following applied:

  • An upper respiratory illness within 14 days before admission.
  • Asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis, or nasal surgery within the past year.
  • Use of intranasal medicines within 14 days before admission.
  • Living with anyone at increased risk from respiratory infection.

sections.title: Removal of Patients from Therapy or Assessment
sections.content: A participant could withdraw consent at any time. The investigator stopped study treatment for an adverse event that made continuation unsafe, for pregnancy, or for a significant protocol deviation. Participants who stopped treatment were asked to complete the follow-up visits. Reasons for not completing are given in section 10.1.

sections.title: Statistical and Analytical Plans
sections.content:
The primary analysis compared the proportion of participants with laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection between arms in the ITT population: the difference in proportions with a Wald 95% confidence interval and a two-sided Fisher's exact test.

Analysis populations: ITT (all randomised participants, analysed as randomised) for efficacy; safety (all participants who received at least one dose, analysed as treated) for safety. Safety data are summarised descriptively; no adjustment for multiplicity was made for secondary endpoints. The formulas are in Appendix 16.1.9.

sections.title: Determination of Sample Size
sections.content: Assuming 60.0% of placebo participants and 20.0% of LMN-301 participants would have the primary endpoint, 20 participants per arm give 75.3% power for a two-sided test at the 0.05 level (normal approximation to the difference in two proportions; formula in Appendix 16.1.9). The assumptions are illustrative.

sections.title: Documentation of statistical methods
sections.content: Difference in proportions: p1 − p2, with a Wald 95% confidence interval, (p1 − p2) ± 1.96 × √(p1(1 − p1)/n1 + p2(1 − p2)/n2). Fisher's exact test: the two-sided p-value sums the probabilities of every 2×2 table with the observed margins that is no more likely than the observed table. Continuous variables: mean, standard deviation (n − 1 denominator), median, minimum and maximum. Percentages use the arm's number of participants in the population analysed. Power of the difference in two proportions (section 9.7.2): Φ((|pa − pb| − 1.96 × √(2p̄(1 − p̄)/n)) / √((pa(1 − pa) + pb(1 − pb))/n)), with p̄ the mean of pa and pb and n per arm.

Synopsis item	Summary
Objectives	To evaluate whether prophylactic intranasal LMN-301 reduces laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after viral challenge compared with placebo. To evaluate the effect of LMN-301 on viral shedding. To describe the safety and local tolerability of intranasal LMN-301.
Design	A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled human viral challenge study conducted in quarantine; intranasal dosing twice daily from the day before challenge to Day 6, quarantine to Day 8 and follow-up to Day 28.
Population	Healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years, seronegative or with a low neutralising titre to the challenge strain. 40 participants were randomised: 20 to Synthetic LMN-301 intranasal, 20 to Placebo intranasal.

Efficacy results	Laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after challenge: Synthetic LMN-301 intranasal: 3/20 (15.0%); Placebo intranasal: 12/20 (60.0%). The difference was -45.0 percentage points (95% CI -71.6 to -18.4; two-sided Fisher's exact p = 0.0079).

Conclusions	Laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after challenge: Synthetic LMN-301 intranasal: 3/20 (15.0%); Placebo intranasal: 12/20 (60.0%). The difference was -45.0 percentage points (95% CI -71.6 to -18.4; two-sided Fisher's exact p = 0.0079). The result favours the investigational product (the interval excludes no difference).

5 · Ethics

The protocol, its amendments, the informed consent form and recruitment material were reviewed and approved by the responsible boards before any participant was enrolled (sections 5.1 to 5.3).

5.1 · Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) or Institutional Review Board (IRB)

5.2 · Ethical Conduct of the Study

The study was conducted in accordance with the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki, ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice, and 21 CFR Parts 50, 56 and 312. The sponsor's monitoring confirmed that each site followed the approved protocol (synthetic statement).

5.3 · Patient Information and Consent

Written informed consent was obtained from each participant before any study procedure, using the board-approved consent form. Participants were told that they could withdraw at any time without giving a reason and without effect on their care.

6 · Investigators and Study Administrative Structure

The study was conducted at the following sites (all fictional):

7 · Introduction

LMN-301 (illustrative): an intranasal spray of spirulina-produced binding proteins intended to neutralise a respiratory virus at the nasal mucosa.

This report describes DEMO-LMN301-P2A-CHAL-001, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled human viral challenge study conducted in quarantine in healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years, seronegative or with a low neutralising titre to the challenge strain. Prevention of viral upper respiratory infection (human challenge model) is the target of the programme; this study was designed to evaluate whether prophylactic intranasal LMN-301 reduces laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after viral challenge compared with placebo.

8 · Study Objectives

Primary objective:

To evaluate whether prophylactic intranasal LMN-301 reduces laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after viral challenge compared with placebo.

Secondary objectives:

To evaluate the effect of LMN-301 on viral shedding.
To describe the safety and local tolerability of intranasal LMN-301.

Exploratory objectives:

To describe body temperature and inflammatory markers after challenge.
9 · Investigational Plan

The investigational plan is described in sections 9.1 to 9.8.

9.1 · Overall Study Design and Plan — Description

A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled human viral challenge study conducted in quarantine, with intranasal dosing twice daily from the day before challenge to Day 6, quarantine to Day 8 and follow-up to Day 28.

Arm	Planned participants	Treatment
Synthetic LMN-301 intranasal	20	Synthetic intranasal dose, twice daily (not actual)
Placebo intranasal	20	Matching placebo spray, twice daily
9.2 · Discussion of Study Design, Including the Choice of Control Groups

A placebo intranasal arm was used so that adverse events and outcomes could be attributed to the investigational product rather than to the course of the condition, the study procedures or expectation. Blinding (section 9.4.6) protects the comparison.

9.3 · Selection of Study Population

The study enrolled healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years, seronegative or with a low neutralising titre to the challenge strain.

9.3.1 · Inclusion Criteria

Participants were eligible if they met all of the following:

Healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years.
A serum neutralising antibody titre to the challenge strain at or below the protocol threshold at screening.
Willing to remain in quarantine from Day -2 to Day 8.
Able to give written informed consent.
9.3.2 · Exclusion Criteria

Participants were not eligible if any of the following applied:

An upper respiratory illness within 14 days before admission.
Asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis, or nasal surgery within the past year.
Use of intranasal medicines within 14 days before admission.
Living with anyone at increased risk from respiratory infection.
9.3.3 · Removal of Patients from Therapy or Assessment

A participant could withdraw consent at any time. The investigator stopped study treatment for an adverse event that made continuation unsafe, for pregnancy, or for a significant protocol deviation. Participants who stopped treatment were asked to complete the follow-up visits. Reasons for not completing are given in section 10.1.

9.4 · Treatments

Treatments are described in sections 9.4.1 to 9.4.8.

9.4.1 · Treatments Administered
Arm	Treatment
Synthetic LMN-301 intranasal	Synthetic intranasal dose, twice daily (not actual)
Placebo intranasal	Matching placebo spray, twice daily

Active: LMN-301 nasal spray, one actuation per nostril twice daily from Day -1 to Day 6 (illustrative). Control: matching placebo spray on the same schedule.

9.4.2 · Identity of Investigational Product(s)

LMN-301 (illustrative): an intranasal spray of spirulina-produced binding proteins intended to neutralise a respiratory virus at the nasal mucosa. Placebo matched the active product in appearance. One synthetic batch of each was used (Appendix 16.1.6).

9.4.3 · Method of Assigning Patients to Treatment Groups

Participants were randomised 1:1 by an interactive response system using permuted blocks of four.

9.4.4 · Selection of Doses in the Study

The dose and regimen are illustrative for this demonstration; in a report for filing this section gives the nonclinical and earlier clinical basis for the doses chosen.

9.4.5 · Selection and Timing of Dose for Each Patient

Doses were taken as described in section 9.4.1 for intranasal dosing twice daily from the day before challenge to Day 6, quarantine to Day 8 and follow-up to Day 28. Missed doses were not replaced.

9.4.6 · Blinding

Participants, investigators, quarantine staff and laboratory staff were blinded; the active and placebo sprays were identical in appearance, smell and taste.

The blind was not broken for any participant before database lock (synthetic statement).

9.4.7 · Prior and Concomitant Therapy

Medicines needed for participants' care were allowed, except those listed as prohibited in the protocol. Concomitant medications recorded during the study:

Treatment compliance was assessed by the sites at each visit. Individual compliance records are not part of the synthetic source; exposure by arm is in section 12.1.

9.5 · Efficacy and Safety Variables

9.5.2 · Appropriateness of Measurements

The efficacy and safety measurements are standard for studies of this kind and are recorded with validated methods at the sites and the central laboratory. Adverse events were coded with MedDRA and medications with the WHO Drug ATC classification.

9.5.3 · Primary Efficacy Variable(s)

Primary endpoint: Laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection after challenge.

Secondary or exploratory: Viral shedding on two or more consecutive days.

9.5.4 · Drug Concentration Measurements

Drug concentrations were not measured in this study, so there is no pharmacokinetic analysis.

9.6 · Data Quality Assurance

Sites were monitored against the protocol and source documents by the CRO, with risk-based monitoring of key indicators. Laboratory tests were run by the central laboratory. Data were entered in an electronic data capture system with edit checks, and the database was locked after all queries were resolved (synthetic statement).

9.7 · Statistical Methods Planned in the Protocol and Determination of Sample Size

The statistical methods are described in sections 9.7.1 and 9.7.2.

9.7.1 · Statistical and Analytical Plans

The primary analysis compared the proportion of participants with laboratory-confirmed symptomatic infection between arms in the ITT population: the difference in proportions with a Wald 95% confidence interval and a two-sided Fisher's exact test.

Analysis populations: ITT (all randomised participants, analysed as randomised) for efficacy; safety (all participants who received at least one dose, analysed as treated) for safety. Safety data are summarised descriptively; no adjustment for multiplicity was made for secondary endpoints. The formulas are in Appendix 16.1.9.

9.7.2 · Determination of Sample Size

Assuming 60.0% of placebo participants and 20.0% of LMN-301 participants would have the primary endpoint, 20 participants per arm give 75.3% power for a two-sided test at the 0.05 level (normal approximation to the difference in two proportions; formula in Appendix 16.1.9). The assumptions are illustrative.

9.8 · Changes in the Conduct of the Study or Planned Analyses

There were no changes to the conduct of the study or to the planned analyses after the first participant was enrolled (synthetic statement).
